item.title: Ackland Film Forum: "Dog Day Afternoon" (Sidney Lumet, 1975) — Mon Sep 28, 7:30 PM — The Lumina Theater
item.description:
Al Pacino and John Cazale lead one of the defining crime films of the 1970s. What begins as a poorly planned Brooklyn bank robbery soon becomes a public spectacle shaped by television cameras, police theatrics, and an increasingly invested crowd. Made in the aftermath of Watergate, the film finds humor, empathy, and absurdity amid a pervasive atmosphere of social distrust. This film will be introduced by Professor Rick Warner, UNC-Chapel Hill Department of English and Comparative Literature, Director of Film Studies. It will be screened at 7:30 p.m. at The Lumina Theater (620 Market St, Chapel Hill, NC 27516). Tickets are free for all audience members, and registration is required via The Lumina’s webpage. When this link is live, click to reserve your free ticket. UNC-Chapel Hill students can receive CLE credit for attending by scanning the QR code at the event.
About the Series: Join the Ackland Film Forum this fall for Socially Charged Crime Thrillers: Snapshots of Social Anx

item.title: Disagree Better University Form — Tue Sep 29, 5:45 PM — Page Auditorium
item.description:

Journalist and Duke alumna Judy Woodruff will serve as moderator. Pre-recorded video remarks by Governor Josh Stein.
Sponsored by Disagree Better and the Provost's Initiative on Pluralism, Free Inquiry, and Belonging, the forum brings leaders from opposing political parties and the campus community together for a live demonstration of civil discourse across differences. Disagree Better is a nonpartisan nonprofit founded by Utah Governor Spencer Cox that works to transform American political culture by elevating healthy conflict as a civic skill - one that strengthens democracy, rebuilds trust, and reduces polarization.
Registration is required and opens September 8.

item.description:
Conflict is inevitable in work, research, and learning environments, and our approach to it determines whether it becomes a source of growth or disruption. This presentation examines the nature of conflict, common assumptions that shape our responses, and the difference between healthy and unhealthy conflict. Attendees will explore various types of conflict and be introduced to a conflict competence model that highlights its emotional, cognitive, and behavioral dimensions. Participants will learn strategies to assess and manage conflict productively, thereby strengthening both individual and team relationships.
Speaker: Jessica Kuchta-Miller, MA, JD, is the Duke University Ombuds. She holds a law degree with a certificate in Dispute Resolution and a master's degree in counseling psychology. item.title: CCN Colloquium: "Mapping the brain’s hidden highways” — Wed Sep 30, 12:00 PM — LSRC - DIBS B035 Multipurpose Room
item.description:
Despite decades of progress in neuroimaging and systems neuroscience, we still lack a wiring diagram of the human brain. This gap reflects fundamental constraints of species and scale: invasive tract-tracing methods cannot be applied in humans, while whole-brain reconstruction in large nonhuman primates remains technically and computationally challenging. As a result, diffusion MRI-based tractography, our primary tool for mapping human white matter, remains only loosely anchored to ground-truth axonal anatomy.
In this talk, I outline an axon-centric strategy for building a biologically informed wiring diagram of the human brain through a coordinated, multimodal and multispecies approach. Leveraging recent advances from the Center for Mesoscale Connectomics, this framework integrates novel types of tract-tracing, polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS OCT), and diffusion MRI across nonhuman primates and humans. item.title: FIP Seminar: Light-sheet microscopy to image across spatiotemporal scales — Wed Sep 30, 12:00 PM — Wilkinson Building
item.description:
Dr. Fiolka is an associate Professor in the Lyda Hill Department of Bioinformatics at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center. Trained as a mechanical engineer in computational fluid dynamics, Dr. Fiolka completed his PhD at the institute of Nanotechnology at ETH Zurich in the group of Dr. Andreas Stemmer. He conducted post-doctoral research at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute's Janelia Research Campus under the late Dr. Mats Gustafsson working on 3D structured illumination microscopy and under Dr. Meng Cui on adaptive optics. At UT Southwestern, the research in his lab aims to extend the current imaging capabilities of optical microscopy such that cancer cell research can be performed in physiologically relevant, 3D environments, ex vivo and in vivo. Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) plays a prominent role in this quest, and in the Fiolka lab, new LSFM methods with improved spatiotemporal resolution are being developed.
Source: Duke University

item.description:
The Thomas Lord Department of Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science hosts Dr. Metin Sitti (Koç University) to present the Pearsall Distinguished Lecture, "Wireless Milli/Microscale Robots for Biomedical Applications."
ABSTRACT: Wireless small-scale medical robots have the unique capability of navigating, operating and staying inside hard-to-reach, tight, risky and deep sites inside our body. This talk reports medical applications of our novel milli- and microscale wireless miniature medical devices and robots down to cell size that could achieve various minimally invasive medical functions, such as targeted active drug delivery, neural stimulation, clot opening, liquid biopsy, biofluid pumping, cauterization, and hyperthermia. Topics include:
• using library databases and finding materials, • special collections and rare book/manuscript research, • copyright and author's rights, • citation and attribution, • practices in the digital humanities, • research impact and metrics, • research data management, • scholarly networks and communities.
This workshop has been approved for two hours of RCR credit and is intended for new graduate students in the arts & humanities.

item.title: An Afternoon with Dartmouth's Dr. Susannah Heschel, Eli Black Distinguished Professor of Jewish Studies — Mon Oct 5, 4:00 PM — Wilson Library
item.description:
Is there a place for Jews and Jewish Study at the American University?
Universities are crucial to the strength and vitality of our country, and Jewish Studies has been foundational for shaping Jewish identity, culture, religion, and politics. Knowledge of Jewish history and thought is the foundation for understanding the meaning and responsibility of Jewish life.
his lecture will trace the rise of the modern university in 19th century Europe and the enthusiastic participation by Jews in academic scholarship as well as the hostility they have encountered at crucial moments. Jewish scholars made extraordinary contributions to the academy, and the field of Jewish Studies changed our understanding of Western civilization.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.description:
Twenty-five years ago, the September 11, 2001, attacks in New York and Washington, D.C. shocked the world. Dramatic changes in American life and foreign policy ensued, including new domestic security measures and the launching of the War on Terror.
Our expert panel will explain how the attacks transformed the United States and the world. Peter Feaver is a political scientist who served in George W. Bush’s White House. Landreth Freeman worked for the CIA for 22 years, specializing in counterintelligence. Chris Kojm spent decades working in US foreign policy and national security and served as deputy director of the 9/11 Commission. Joseph Stieb is a historian of U.S. military and foreign policy. Historian Michael Morgan will moderate the discussion.

Dec 10, 2026 9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-december-10-2026)**
**Your mAP is fine. Your slices are not. Finding the images that actually matter**
A single mAP can look acceptable while one slice is unusable, small objects, occlusion, or a confused class. I will run a pretrained detector on a few hundred public images (COCO-style, not a production crawl), report the headline metric, then break the same run by slice and walk through the worst samples.
The claim is modest: you do not need a million images or a trained-from-scratch model to see what the mean is hiding, and you cannot relabel everything, so the next labeling budget should follow those slices. No employer data and no confidential dashboards.

item.title: The Gift of a Corpse: Ordinary Necropolitics in Contemporary Singapore — Tue Sep 29, 3:00 PM — Friedl 225
item.description:
Anthropologist and mortician, Ruth E. Toulson, takes you behind the scenes in a Singaporean funeral parlor.
While multiple authors have probed the corpse's power as a potent political symbol, much of the existing literature on necropolitics has an exclusive focus on contexts of violent regime change, on the bodies of political leaders, or of "the dead" understood as an undifferentiated mass.
In Singapore, in contrast, Toulson argues that the manipulation of corpses is a quotidian strategy of political power, part of the everyday actions of a stable state. What's more, the corpses this state puts to its use are those of ordinary people, whose unremarkable deaths are marked in what seem initially to be unremarkable ways.

Join us as DJ Synko heats up the dance floor with classic salsa, merengue, and bachata from 8-10pm, mixing in the best of reggaeton, perrea, Latin house, dembow, cumbia, and more from 10pm to 1:30am. Show off your moves, or just vibe to the music and enjoy creative cocktails and great company on the roof. Drink specials, no cover, 21+ with valid ID to enter. Come early to beat the line – if you know, you know!
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: House of Heavy — Fri Oct 2, 8:30 PM — Stanczyks
item.description:
House of Heavy is a night built for the fans who crave the pit, the riffs, the breakdowns, and the chaos, but are tired of waiting for the next metal tour to hit their city. We’re bringing the energy of a packed metal show to you all year long: the nu-metal nostalgia, the alt-metal anthems, the metal-core breakdowns. Come scream along, throw down with friends, and lose yourself in the heaviest night out your city has to offer
Source: Downtown Durham Inc
